newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Baoshi set to list A shares in Shenzhen.
newsitem.headline: Baoshi set to list A shares in Shenzhen.

text.p: Hebei-based Shijiazhuang Baoshi Electronic Co Ltd said on Monday it had received approval from the Shenzhen stock exchange to list 26.20 million class A shares and 3.7779 million shares for employees on September 25.
The securities code for the A shares has been set as "0413.SZ," Baoshi said in a listing notice published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.

The 26.20 million A shares were issued at 6.28 yuan per share via the Shenzhen exchange's automated quotation system earlier this month, while the staff shares were offered at 1.50 yuan each in 1992, Baoshi said.
Shanghai Shenyin & Wanguo Securities and Pingan Securities have been named the listing promoters, said Baoshi, which specialises in making black-and-white television tubes and related components.
Baoshi, which already has 100 million class B shares listed in Shenzhen, said it plans to funnel the proceeds from the A share offer into manufacturing colour television tubes.
Baoshi's B share offer prospectus said that under international accounting standards, it racked up 170.17 million yuan in after-tax profits in 1995, compared with 116.16 million yuan in 1994.
Baoshi reported 1996 interim unaudited net earnings results, under international accounting standards, of 65.66 million yuan, down 20.7 percent from the year earlier level of 82.75 million.

Prior to the A share offer, Baoshi had a total share capital of 356.80 million shares, including 233.4105 million founder shares, 100 million B shares, 4.50 million legal person shares and 18.8895 million staff shares.
The 100 million B shares were offered at HK$1.99 per share earlier this year and were listed in July.

Baoshi, based in Shijiazhuang, the capital of central Hebei province, was jointly set up by the Shijiazhuang Television Tube actory, China Electronics Import and Export General Co and Zhonghua Hebei Import and Export Co in 1992.

Baoshi said in its B share offer prospectus that most of its products are sold in rural areas of China, and added that it plans to export black-and-white television tubes to such developing countries as Egypt, India and Pakistan.
